question: Malavikagnimitra, a drama of the 5th century CE, was written by _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalidasa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa,** a prominent figure in classical Sanskrit literature, authored the renowned play **"Mālavikāgnimitram" **during the **5th century CE**.
 
• Set in the backdrop of Pushyamitra Shunga's reign, the five-act drama revolves around King Agnimitra's affection for Mālavikā, the maid of his chief queen.
 
• Its captivating storyline, the play is also esteemed as a comprehensive discourse on dramatic art, featuring intricate details such as the Rajasuya sacrifice and insightful theories on music and acting.
 
• Kalidasa himself, a luminary of the Gupta era, is best known for his contributions to Sanskrit literature, which primarily draw from Hindu Puranic narratives and philosophical themes.
 
• His literary legacy encompasses three plays, two epic poems, and two shorter compositions, showcasing his mastery over various genres within Sanskrit literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Acharya Pingala,** an ancient Indian poet and mathematician, left a significant mark with his seminal work "Chandaḥśāstra," also known as the Pingala-sutras. This treatise, composed in the late Sūtra style, delves into Sanskrit prosody across eight chapters, although its full comprehension often necessitates supplementary commentary.
 
• **Harisena**, a distinguished Sanskrit poet and court official in the 4th century, held a prominent position in the court of Gupta emperor Samudragupta. His most acclaimed composition, composed around 345 CE, is an ode to the valor of Samudragupta, immortalized on the Allahabad Pillar.
 
• **Bhavabhūti**, an eminent scholar from the 8th century, earned renown for his plays and poetry composed in Sanskrit. Often hailed as the counterpart to Kalidasa, his works, particularly the "Uttararamacarita," showcase his expertise in evoking the sentiment of compassion, earning him the epithet "Poet of Karun Rasa."
